Some think this was fulfilled in those whom he miraculously raised to life, Jairus's daughter, the widow's son, and Lazarus; and it is observable that all whom Christ raised were spoken to, as, Damsel, arise; Young man, arise; Lazarus, come forth; whereas those raised under the Old Testament were raised, not by a word, but other applications, Kg1 17:21; Kg2 4:34; Kg2 13:21. Some understand it of those saints that rose with Christ; but we do not read of the voice of the Son of God calling them. But, 2. I rather understand it of the power of the doctrine of Christ, for the recovering and quickening of those that were dead in trespasses and sins, Eph 2:1. The hour was coming when dead souls should be made alive by the preaching of the gospel, and a spirit of life from God accompanying it: nay, it then was, while Christ was upon earth. It may refer especially to the calling of the Gentiles, which is said to be as life from the dead, and, some think, was prefigured by Ezekiel's vision (Eze 37:1), and foretold, Isa 26:19. Thy dead men shall live. But it is to be applied to all the wonderful success of the gospel, among both Jews and Gentiles; an hour which still is, and is still coming, till all the elect be effectually called. Note, (1.) Sinners are spiritually dead, destitute of spiritual life, sense, strength, and motion, dead to God, miserable, but neither sensible of their misery nor able to help themselves out of it. (2.) The conversion of a soul to God is its resurrection from death to life; then it begins to live when it begins to live to God, to breathe after him, and move towards him. (3.) It is by the voice of the Son of God that souls are raised to spiritual life; it is wrought by his power, and that power conveyed and communicated by his word: The dead shall hear, shall be made to hear, to understand, receive, and believe, the voice of the Son of God, to hear it as his voice; then the Spirit by it gives life, otherwise the letter kills. (4.) The voice of Christ must be heard by us, that we may live by it. They that hear, and attend to what they hear, shall live. Hear and your soul shall live, Isa 55:3.
Secondly, A resurrection yet to come; this is spoken of, Joh 5:28, Joh 5:29, introduced with, "Marvel not at this, which I have said of the first resurrection, do not reject it as incredible and absurd, for at the end of time you shall all see a more sensible and amazing proof of the power and authority of the Son of man." As his own resurrection was reserved to be the final and concluding proof of his personal commission, so the resurrection of all men is reserved to be a like proof of his commission to be executed by his spirit. Now observe here,
a. When this resurrection shall be: The hour is coming; it is fixed to an hour, so very punctual is this great appointment. The judgment is not adjourned sine die - to some time not yet pitched upon; no, he hath appointed a day. The hour is coming. (a.) It is not yet come, it is not the hour spoken of at Joh 5:25, that is coming, and now is. Those erred dangerously who said that the resurrection was past already, Ti2 2:18, But, (b.) It will certainly come, it is coming on, nearer every day than other; it is at the door. How far off it is we know not; but we know that it is infallibly designed and unalterably determined.
b. Who shall be raised: All that are in the graves, all that have died from the beginning of time, and all that shall die to the end of time. It was said (Dan 12:2), Many shall arise; Christ here tells us that those many shall be all; all must appear before the Judge, and therefore all must be raised; every person, and the whole of every person; every soul shall return to its body, and every bone to its bone. The grave is the prison of dead bodies, where they are detained; their furnace, where they are consumed (Job 24:19); yet, in prospect of their resurrection, we may call it their bed, where they sleep to be awaked again; their treasury, where they are laid up to be used again. Even those that are not put into graves shall arise; but, because most are put into graves, Christ uses this expression, all that are in the graves. The Jews used the word sheol for the grave, which signifies the state of the dead; all that are in that state shall hear.
c. How they shall be raised. Two things are here told us: - (a.) The efficient of this resurrection: They shall hear his voice; that is, he shall cause them to hear it, as Lazarus was made to hear that word, Come forth; a divine power shall go along with the voice, to put life into them, and enable them to obey it. When Christ rose, there was no voice heard, not a word spoken, because he rose by his own power; but at the resurrection of the children of men we find three voices spoken of, Th1 4:16. The Lord shall descend with a shout, the shout of a king, with the voice of the archangel; either Christ himself, the prince of the angels, or the commander-in-chief, under him, of the heavenly hosts; and with the trumpet of God: the soldier's trumpet sounding the alarm of war, the judge's trumpet publishing the summons to the court. (b.) The effect of it: They shall come forth out of their graves, as prisoners out of their prison-house; they shall arise out of the dust, and shake themselves from it; see Isa 52:1, Isa 52:2, Isa 52:11. But this is not all; they shall appear before Christ's tribunal, shall come forth as those that are to be tried, come forth to the bar, publicly to receive their doom.
d. To what they shall be raised; to a different state of happiness or misery, according to their different character; to a state of retribution, according to what they did in the state of probation.
(a.) They that have done good shall come forth to the resurrection of life; they shall live again, to live for ever. Note, [a.] Whatever name men are called by, or whatever plausible profession they make, it will be well in the great day with those only that have done good, have done that which is pleasing to God and profitable to others. [b.] The resurrection of the body will be a resurrection of life to all those, and those only, that have been sincere and constant in doing good. They shall not only be publicly acquitted, as a pardoned criminal, we say, has his life, but they shall be admitted into the presence of God, and that is life, it is better than life; they shall be attended with comforts in perfection. To live is to be happy, and they shall be advanced above the fear of death; that is life indeed in which mortality is for ever swallowed up.
(b.) They that have done evil to the resurrection of damnation; they shall live again, to be for ever dying. The Pharisees thought that the resurrection pertained only to the just, but Christ here rectifies that mistake. Note, [a.] Evil doers, whatever they pretend, will be treated in the day of judgment as evil men. [b.] The resurrection will be to evil doers, who did not by repentance undo what they had done amiss, a resurrection of damnation. They shall come forth to be publicly convicted of rebellion against God, and publicly condemned to everlasting punishment; to be sentenced to it, and immediately sent to it without reprieve. Such will the resurrection be.
(2.) Observe what is here said concerning the Mediator's authority to execute judgment, Joh 5:22-24, Joh 5:27. As he has an almighty power, so he has a sovereign jurisdiction; and who so fit to preside in the great affairs of the other life as he who is the Father and fountain of life? Here is,
[1.] Christ's commission or delegation to the office of a judge, which is twice spoken of here (Joh 5:22): He hath committed all judgment to the Son; and again (Joh 5:27): he hath given him authority.
First, The Father judges no man; not that the Father hath resigned the government, but he is pleased to govern by Jesus Christ; so that man is not under the terror of dealing with God immediately, but has the comfort of access to him by a Mediator. Having made us, he may do what he pleases with us, as the potter with the clay; yet he does not take advantage of this, but draws us with the cords of a man. 2. He does not determine our everlasting condition by the covenant of innocency, nor take the advantage he has against us for the violation of that covenant. The Mediator having undertaken to make a vicarious satisfaction, the matter is referred to him, and God is willing to enter upon a new treaty; not under the law of the Creator, but the grace of the Redeemer.
Secondly, He has committed all judgment to the Son, has constituted him Lord of all (Act 10:36; Rom 14:9), as Joseph in Egypt, Gen 41:40. This was prophesied of, Psa 72:1; Isa 11:3, Isa 11:4; Jer 23:5; Mic 5:1-4; Psa 67:4; Psa 96:13; Psa 98:9. All judgment is committed to our Lord Jesus; for 1. He is entrusted with the administration of the providential kingdom, is head over all things (Eph 1:11), head of every man, Co1 11:3. All things consist by him, Col 1:17. 2. He is empowered to make laws immediately to bind conscience. I say unto you is now the form in which the statues of the kingdom of heaven run. Be it enacted by the Lord Jesus, and by his authority. All the acts now in force are touched with his sceptre. 3. He is authorized to appoint and settle the terms of the new covenant, and to draw up the articles of peace between God and man; it is God in Christ that reconciles the world, and to him he has given power to confer eternal life. The book of life is the Lamb's book; by his award we must stand or fall. 4. He is commissioned to carry on and complete the war with the powers of darkness; to cast out and give judgment against the prince of this world, Joh 12:31. He is commissioned not only to judge, but to make war, Rev 19:11. All that will fight for God against Satan must enlist themselves under his banner. 5. He is constituted sole manager of the judgment of the great day. The ancients generally understood these words of that crowning act of his judicial power. The final and universal judgment is committed to the Son of man; the tribunal is his, it is the judgment-seat of Christ; the retinue is his, his mighty angels; he will try the causes, and pass the sentence. Act 17:31.
Thirdly, He has given him authority to execute judgment also, Joh 5:27. Observe, 1. What the authority is which our Redeemer is invested with: An authority to execute judgment; he has not only a legislative and judicial power, but an executive power too. The phrase here is used particularly for the judgment of condemnation, Jde 1:15. poiēsai krisin - to execute judgment upon all; the same with his taking vengeance, Th2 1:8. The ruin of impenitent sinners comes from the hand of Christ; he that executes judgment upon them is the same that would have wrought salvation for them, which makes the sentence unexceptionable; and there is no relief against the sentence of the Redeemer; salvation itself cannot save those whom the Saviour condemns, which makes the ruin remediless. 2. Whence he has that authority: the Father gave it to him. Christ's authority as Mediator is delegated and derived; he acts as the Father's Viceregent, as the Lord's Anointed, the Lord's Christ. Now all this redounds very much to the honour of Christ, acquitting him from the guilt of blasphemy, in making himself equal with God; and very much to the comfort of all believers, who may with the greatest assurance venture their all in such hands.
[2.] Here are the reasons (reasons of state) for which this commission was given him. He has all judgment committed to him for two reasons: - 
First, Because he is the Son of man; which denotes these three things: - 1. His humiliation and gracious condescension. Man is a worm, the son of man a worm; yet this was the nature, this the character, which the Redeemer assumed, in pursuance of the counsels of love; to this low estate he stooped, and submitted to all the mortifications attending it, because it was his Father's will; in recompence therefore of this wonderful obedience, God did thus dignify him. Because he condescended to be the Son of man, his Father made him Lord of all, Phi 2:8, Phi 2:9. 2. His affinity and alliance to us. The Father has committed the government of the children of men to him, because, being the Son of man, he is of the same nature with those whom he is set over, and therefore the more unexceptionable, and the more acceptable, as a Judge. Their governor shall proceed from the midst of them, Jer 30:21. Of this that law was typical; One of thy brethren shalt thou set king over thee, Deu 17:15. 3. His being the Messiah promised. In that famous vision of his kingdom and glory, Dan 7:13, Dan 7:14, he is called the Son of man; and Psa 8:4-6. Thou has made the Son of man have dominion over the works of thy hands. He is the Messiah, and therefore is invested with all this power. The Jews usually called the Christ the Son of David; but Christ usually called himself the Son of man, which was the more humble title, and bespeaks him a prince and Saviour, not the Jewish nation only, but to the whole race of mankind.
Secondly, That all men should honour the Son, Joh 5:23. The honouring of Jesus Christ is here spoken of as God's great design (the Son intended to glorify the Father, and therefore the Father intended to glorify the Son, Joh 12:32); and as man's great duty, in compliance with that design. If God will have the Son honoured, it is the duty of all to whom he is made known to honour him. Observe here, 1. The respect that is to be paid to our Lord Jesus: We must honour the Son, must look upon him as one that is to be honoured, both on account of his transcendent excellences and perfections in himself, and of the relations he stands in to us, and must study to give him honour accordingly; must confess that he is Lord, and worship him; must honour him who was dishonoured for us. 2. The degree of it: Even as they honour the Father. This supposes it to be our duty to honour the Father; for revealed religion is founded on natural religion, and directs us to honour the Son, to honour him with divine honour; we must honour the Redeemer with the same honour with which we honour the Creator. So far was it from blasphemy for him to make himself equal with God that it is the highest injury that can be for us to make him otherwise. The truths and laws of the Christian religion, so far as they are revealed, are as sacred and honourable as those of natural religion, and to be equally had in estimation; for we lie under the same obligations to Christ, the Author of our being; and have as necessary a dependence upon the Redeemer's grace as upon the Creator's providence, which is a sufficient ground for this law - to honour the Son as we honour the Father. To enforce this law, it is added, He that honours not the Son honours not the Father who has sent him. Some pretend a reverence for the Creator, and speak honourably of him, who make light of the Redeemer, and speak contemptibly of him; but let such know that the honours and interests of the Father and Son are so inseparably twisted and interwoven that the Father never reckons himself honoured by any that dishonour the Son. Note, (1.) Indignities done to the Lord Jesus reflect upon God himself, and will so be construed and reckoned for in the court of heaven. The Son having so far espoused the Father's honour as to take to himself the reproaches cast on him (Rom 15:3), the Father does no less espouse the Son's honour, and counts himself struck at through him. (2.) The reason of this is because the Son is sent and commissioned by the Father; it is the Father who hath sent him. Affronts to an ambassador are justly resented by the prince that sends him. And by this rule those who truly honour the Son honour the Father also; see Phi 2:11.
[3.] Here is the rule by which the Son goes in executing this commission, so those words seem to come in (Joh 5:24): He that heareth and believeth hath everlasting life. Here we have the substance of the whole gospel; the preface commands attention to a thing most weighty, and assent to a thing most certain: "Verily, verily, I say unto you, I, to whom you hear all judgment is committed, I, in whose lips is a divine sentence; take from me the Christian's character and charter."
First, The character of a Christian: He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me. To be a Christian indeed is, 1. To hear the word of Christ. It is not enough to be within hearing of it, but we must attend on it, as scholars on the instructions of their teachers; and attend to it, as servants to the commands of their masters; we must hear and obey it, must abide by the gospel of Christ as the fixed rule of our faith and practice. 2. To believe on him that sent him; for Christ's design is to bring us to God; and, as he is the first original of all grace, so is he the last object of all faith. Christ is our way; God is our rest. We must believe on God as having sent Jesus Christ, and recommended himself to our faith and love, by manifesting his glory in the face of Jesus Christ (Co2 4:6), as his Father and our Father.
Secondly, The charter of a Christian, in which all that are Christians indeed are interested. See what we get by Christ. 1. A charter of pardon: He shall not come into condemnation. The grace of the gospel is a full discharge from the curse of the law. A believer shall not only not lie under condemnation eternally, but shall not come into condemnation now, not come into the danger of it (Rom 8:1), not come into judgment, not be so much as arraigned. 2. A charter of privileges: He is passed out of death to life, is invested in a present happiness in spiritual life and entitled to a future happiness in eternal life. The tenour of the first covenant was, Do this and live; the man that doeth them shall live in them. Now this proves Christ equal with the Father that he has power to propose the same benefit to the hearers of his word that had been proposed to the keepers of the old law, that is, life: Hear and live, believe and live, is what we may venture our souls upon, when we are disabled to do and live; see Joh 17:2.
[4.] Here is the righteousness of his proceedings pursuant to this commission, Joh 5:30. All judgment being committed to him, we cannot but ask how he manages it. And here he answers, My judgment is just. All Christ
b16.es:
Tenemos aquí el discurso de Cristo en ocasión de ser acusado de violar el sábado, y parece ser su reivindicación de sí mismo ante el sanedrín, cuando fue procesado ante ellos: no aparece si el mismo día, o dos o tres días después; probablemente el mismo día. observar,
I. La doctrina establecida, por la cual justificó lo que hizo en el día de reposo (Juan 5:17): Les respondió. Esto supone que se le había imputado algo: o lo que se sugirieron unos a otros, cuando querían matarlo (Juan 5:16), él lo supo, y dio esta respuesta: Mi Padre hasta ahora trabaja, y yo trabajo. En otras ocasiones, en respuesta a una acusación similar, había alegado el ejemplo de que David comía los panes de la proposición, de que los sacerdotes sacrificaban los sacrificios y de que el pueblo daba de beber a su ganado en el día de reposo; pero aquí va más allá y alega el ejemplo de su Padre y su autoridad divina; renunciando a todos los demás argumentos, insiste en lo que era instar omnium - equivalente al todo, y se atiene a ello, que había mencionado, Mateo 12:8. El Hijo del hombre es Señor incluso del día del sábado; pero aquí lo amplía. 1. Él alega que era el Hijo de Dios, claramente insinuado al llamar a Dios su Padre; y, de ser así, su santidad era incuestionable y su soberanía indiscutible; y podría hacer las modificaciones que quisiera de la ley divina. Seguramente reverenciarán al Hijo, el heredero de todas las cosas. 2. Que era un trabajador junto con Dios. (1.) Mi Padre trabaja hasta ahora. El ejemplo del descanso de Dios de toda su obra en el séptimo día es, en el cuarto mandamiento, la base para que lo observemos como un sábado o día de descanso. Ahora Dios descansó sólo del trabajo que había hecho los seis días anteriores; de lo contrario, hasta ahora trabaja, trabaja todos los días, los días de reposo y los días de semana, sosteniendo y gobernando a todas las criaturas, y concurriendo por su providencia común a todos los movimientos y operaciones de la naturaleza, para su propia gloria; por lo tanto, cuando se nos designa descansar en el día de reposo, no se nos impide hacer aquello que tiene una tendencia directa a la gloria de Dios, como lo hizo el hombre que llevaba su cama. (2.) trabajo; Por tanto, no sólo puedo trabajar, como él, para hacer el bien tanto en los días de reposo como en los demás días, sino que también trabajo con él. Así como Dios creó todas las cosas por medio de Cristo, así sostiene y gobierna todas las cosas por él, Heb 1:3.

Esto sitúa lo que hace por encima de toda excepción; el que es tan gran trabajador debe ser necesariamente un gobernador incontrolable; el que hace todo es Señor de todo, y por lo tanto Señor del sábado, rama particular de su autoridad que ahora afirmaría, porque pronto iba a mostrarla más, en el cambio del día del séptimo al primero. II. La ofensa que se tomó contra su doctrina (Juan 5:18): Los judíos procuraban más matarlo. Su defensa se convirtió en su ofensiva, como si al justificarse hubiera empeorado las cosas. Tenga en cuenta que aquellos que no sean iluminados por la palabra de Cristo se enfurecerán y exasperarán por ella, y nada irrita más a los enemigos de Cristo que el hecho de que él afirme su autoridad; ver Salmo 2:3-5. Intentaron matarlo,
1. Porque había quebrantado el sábado; porque, diga lo que quiera en su propia justificación, están resueltos, con razón o sin ella, a declararlo culpable de violar el sábado. Cuando la malicia y la envidia se sientan en el estrado, la razón y la justicia pueden incluso guardar silencio ante el tribunal, porque todo lo que puedan decir será indudablemente anulado. 2. No sólo eso, sino que también había dicho que Dios era su Padre. Ahora fingen tener celos por el honor de Dios, como antes por el día de reposo, y acusan a Cristo de ser un crimen atroz por haberse hecho igual a Dios; y hubiera sido un crimen atroz si realmente no lo hubiera sido. Fue pecado de Lucifer, seré como el Altísimo. Ahora bien, (1.) Esto se infirió con razón de lo que dijo, que él era el Hijo de Dios, y que Dios era su Padre, patera idion - su propio Padre; suyo, como si no fuera de nadie más. Había dicho que trabajaba con su Padre, con la misma autoridad y poder, y por eso se hacía igual a Dios. Ecee intelligunt Judaei, quod non intelligunt Ariani - He aquí, los judíos entienden lo que los arrianos no entienden. (2.) Sin embargo, se le imputó injustamente como una ofensa el hecho de igualarse a Dios, porque él era y es Dios, igual al Padre (Filipenses 2:6); y por lo tanto Cristo, en respuesta a esta acusación, no excepto contra la insinuación por forzada o forzada, presenta su reclamo y prueba que es igual a Dios en poder y gloria. III. El discurso de Cristo en esta ocasión, que continúa sin interrupción hasta el final del capítulo. En estos versos explica, y luego confirma, su comisión, como Mediador y plenipotenciario en el tratado entre Dios y el hombre.

Y, así como los honores a los que tiene derecho son tales que ninguna criatura puede recibirlos, así también la obra que se le confía es tal que ninguna criatura puede realizarla, y por lo tanto él es Dios, igual al Padre. 1. En general. Él es uno con el Padre en todo lo que hace como Mediador, y hubo un perfecto entendimiento entre ellos en todo el asunto. Se inicia con un prefacio solemne (Juan 5:19): De cierto, de cierto os digo; Yo el Amén, el Amén, lo digo. Esto da a entender que las cosas declaradas son: (1.) Muy terribles y grandiosas, y que deberían merecer la más seria atención. (2.) Muy seguro, y que debería exigir un asentimiento sincero. (3.) Que son asuntos puramente de revelación divina; cosas que Cristo nos ha dicho y que de otro modo no podríamos haber llegado a conocer. Dos cosas dice en general acerca de la unidad del Hijo con el Padre en la obra: - 
[1.] Que el Hijo se conforma al Padre (Juan 5:19): El Hijo no puede hacer nada por sí mismo sino lo que ve hacer al Padre; porque estas cosas hace el Hijo. El Señor Jesús, como Mediador, es Primero, Obediente a la voluntad de su Padre; tan enteramente obediente que no puede hacer nada por sí mismo, en el mismo sentido en que se dice, Dios no puede mentir, no puede negarse a sí mismo, lo que expresa la perfección de su verdad, no ninguna imperfección en su fuerza; así que aquí Cristo estaba tan enteramente dedicado a la voluntad de su Padre que le era imposible actuar por separado en cualquier cosa. En segundo lugar, Él observa el consejo de su Padre; no puede y no hará nada más que lo que ve hacer al Padre. Ningún hombre puede descubrir la obra de Dios, pero el Hijo unigénito, que yacía en su seno, ve lo que hace, conoce íntimamente sus propósitos y tiene su plan siempre ante sí. Lo que hizo como Mediador, a lo largo de toda su empresa, fue la transcripción o contrapartida exacta de lo que hizo el Padre; es decir, lo que él diseñó, cuando formó el plan de nuestra redención en sus consejos eternos, y estableció esas medidas en todo lo que nunca podría romperse ni necesitar ser alterado. Era la copia de ese gran original; Fue la fidelidad de Cristo, como lo fue la de Moisés, que hizo todo según el modelo que se le mostró en el monte.

Esto se expresa en tiempo presente, lo que ve hacer al Padre, por la misma razón que, cuando estuvo aquí en la tierra, se dijo: Está en los cielos (Jn 3:13), y está en el seno del Padre (Jn 1:18); Como ya entonces estaba presente en el cielo por su naturaleza divina, así las cosas hechas en el cielo estaban presentes en su conocimiento. Lo que el Padre hizo en sus consejos, el Hijo siempre lo tuvo presente, y todavía tenía sus ojos puestos en ello, como David en espíritu habló de él: Al Señor siempre he puesto delante de mí, Salmo 16:8. En tercer lugar, sin embargo, él es igual al Padre en obrar; porque todo lo que hace el Padre, también lo hace el Hijo de la misma manera; hacía las mismas cosas, no tales cosas, sino tauta, las mismas cosas; y las hacía de la misma manera, homoiōs, igualmente, con la misma autoridad, y libertad, y sabiduría, la misma energía y eficacia. ¿El Padre promulga, deroga y modifica leyes positivas? ¿Domina el curso de la naturaleza, conoce los corazones de los hombres? También el Hijo. El poder del Mediador es un poder divino. [2.] Que el Padre comunica al Hijo, Juan 5:20. observar,
Primero, el incentivo para ello: el Padre ama al Hijo; Él declaró: Este es mi Hijo amado. No sólo tenía buena voluntad para la empresa, sino también una infinita complacencia en el empresario. Cristo ahora era odiado por los hombres, a quien la nación aborrecía (Isaías 49:7); pero él se consolaba con esto: que su Padre lo amaba. En segundo lugar, sus ejemplos. Lo muestra, 1. En lo que le comunica: Le muestra todas las cosas que él mismo hace. Las medidas del Padre al hacer y gobernar el mundo se muestran al Hijo, para que él pueda tomar las mismas medidas al formar y gobernar la iglesia, cuya obra iba a ser un duplicado de la obra de la creación y la providencia, y por lo tanto es llamada el mundo venidero. Le muestra todas las cosas ha autos poiei, lo que él hace, es decir, lo que hace el Hijo, para que pueda ser interpretado; todo lo que hace el Hijo es por dirección del Padre; él le muestra. 2. En lo que comunicará; él le mostrará, es decir, lo nombrará y dirigirá para que haga obras mayores que estas. (1.) Obras de mayor poder que la curación del impotente; porque él resucitaría a los muertos, y él mismo resucitaría de entre los muertos. Por el poder de la naturaleza, con el uso de medios, es posible que con el tiempo se pueda curar una enfermedad; pero la naturaleza nunca puede, por el uso de ningún medio, resucitar a los muertos en ningún momento.

(2.) Obras de mayor autoridad que garantizar que el hombre cargue su cama en el día de reposo. Pensaron que se trataba de un intento atrevido; pero ¿qué significaba esto para que él derogara toda la ley ceremonial e instituyera nuevas ordenanzas, que pronto haría, "para que os maravilléis"? Ahora miraban sus obras con desprecio e indignación, pero pronto hará lo que ellos mirarán con asombro, Lucas 7:16. Muchos se maravillan de las obras de Cristo, por las cuales él tiene el honor de ellos, a quienes no se les hace creer, por lo que obtendrían el beneficio de ellas. 2. En particular. Él demuestra su igualdad con el Padre especificando algunas de las obras que realiza y que son obras peculiares de Dios. Esto se amplía, Juan 5:21-30. Él hace, y hará, lo que es la obra peculiar del dominio y jurisdicción soberanos de Dios: juzgar y ejecutar juicio, Juan 5:22-24, Juan 5:27. Estos dos están entrelazados, casi conectados; y lo que se dice una vez se repite e inculca; juntemos ambas cosas, y probaremos que Cristo no dijo mal cuando se hizo igual a Dios. (1.) Observe lo que se dice aquí sobre el poder del Mediador para resucitar a los muertos y dar vida. Ver [1.] Su autoridad para hacerlo (Juan 5:21): Como el Padre resucita a los muertos, así el Hijo da vida a quien quiere. Primero, es prerrogativa de Dios resucitar a los muertos y darle vida, incluso a aquel que primero sopló en el hombre aliento de vida, y así lo hizo alma viviente; ver Deuteronomio 32:30; Sa 1 2:6; Salmo 68:20; Romanos 4:17. Esto Dios lo había hecho por medio de los profetas Elías y Eliseo, y fue una confirmación de su misión. Una resurrección de entre los muertos nunca estuvo en el camino común de la naturaleza, ni jamás cayó dentro del pensamiento de aquellos que estudiaron sólo el alcance del poder de la naturaleza, uno de cuyos axiomas recibidos estaba en contra de ella: A privatione ad habitum non datur regressus - La existencia, una vez extinguida, no puede reavivarse. Por lo tanto, fue ridiculizado en Atenas como algo absurdo, Hechos 17:32. Es puramente obra de un poder divino, y su conocimiento puramente por revelación divina. Esto lo poseerían los judíos. En segundo lugar, el Mediador tiene esta prerrogativa: vivifica a quien quiere; resucita a quien quiere y cuando quiere.

No da vida a las cosas por necesidad natural, como lo hace el sol, cuyos rayos, por supuesto, reviven; pero actúa como un agente libre, tiene la administración de su poder en sus propias manos y nunca se ve obligado o restringido en su uso. Así como tiene el poder, también tiene la sabiduría y la soberanía de un Dios; tiene la llave del sepulcro y de la muerte (Apocalipsis 1:18), no como un siervo, para abrir y cerrar como se le ordena, porque la tiene como la llave de David, del cual él es dueño, Apocalipsis 3:7. Un príncipe absoluto se describe así (Daniel 5:19): a quien mataría o mantendría con vida; es cierto de Cristo sin hipérbole. [2.] Su capacidad para hacerlo. Por tanto, tiene poder para vivificar a quien quiere, como el Padre, porque tiene vida en sí mismo, como la tiene el Padre, Juan 5:26. Primero, es cierto que el Padre tiene vida en sí mismo. No sólo es un Ser autoexistente, que no deriva de Rom. o depender de cualquier otro (Éxodo 3:14), pero él es un soberano dador de vida; tiene en sí mismo la disposición de la vida; y de todo bien (porque así a veces significa la vida); todo se deriva de él y depende de él. Él es para sus criaturas la fuente de la vida y de todo bien; autor de su ser y bienestar; el Dios vivo, y el Dios de todos los vivientes. En segundo lugar, es igualmente cierto que le ha dado al Hijo el tener vida en sí mismo. Así como el Padre es el original de toda vida y bien natural, siendo el gran Creador, así el Hijo, como Redentor, es el original de toda vida y bien espiritual; es eso para la iglesia lo que el Padre es para el mundo; ver 1 Col 8:6; Col 1:19. El reino de la gracia, y toda la vida en ese reino, están tan plena y absolutamente en manos del Redentor como el reino de la providencia está en manos del Creador; y como Dios, que da ser a todas las cosas, tiene su ser por sí mismo, así Cristo, que da vida, resucitó a la vida por su propio poder, Juan 10:18. [3.] Su actuación de acuerdo con esta autoridad y capacidad. Teniendo vida en sí mismo y estando autorizado para vivificar a quien quiera, en virtud de esto hay, por consiguiente, dos resurrecciones realizadas por su poderosa palabra, de las cuales se habla aquí: 
Primero, una resurrección que ahora es (Juan 5:29), una resurrección de la muerte del pecado a la vida de justicia, por el poder de la gracia de Cristo. La hora está llegando, y ahora es.

Es una resurrección que ya ha comenzado y que continuará cuando los muertos oigan la voz del Hijo de Dios. Esto se distingue claramente de lo de Juan 5:28, que habla de la resurrección al final de los tiempos. Esto no dice nada, como sí lo hace, de los muertos en sus gracias, y de todos ellos, y de su salida a la luz. Ahora bien, 1. Algunos piensan que esto se cumplió en aquellos a quienes resucitó milagrosamente, la hija de Jairo, el hijo de la viuda y Lázaro; y es observable que a todos los que Cristo resucitó se les habló como: Damisela, levántate; Joven, levántate; Lázaro, sal; mientras que los resucitados bajo el Antiguo Testamento fueron resucitados, no por una palabra, sino por otras aplicaciones, 1 Reyes 17:21; Reyes 4:34; Reyes 13:21. Algunos lo entienden de aquellos santos que resucitaron con Cristo; pero no leemos de la voz del Hijo de Dios llamándolos. Pero, 2. Más bien lo entiendo del poder de la doctrina de Cristo, para la recuperación y vivificación de los que estaban muertos en delitos y pecados, Efesios 2:1. Se acercaba la hora en que las almas muertas deberían ser vivificadas por la predicación del evangelio, y un espíritu de vida de Dios que lo acompañara; más aún, así fue entonces, mientras Cristo estaba en la tierra. Puede referirse especialmente al llamamiento de los gentiles, que se dice que es como vida de entre los muertos y, según piensan algunos, fue prefigurado por la visión de Ezequiel (Ezequiel 37:1) y predicho, Isaías 26:19. Tus muertos vivirán. Pero debe aplicarse a todo el maravilloso éxito del evangelio, tanto entre judíos como entre gentiles; una hora que aún es y aún llega, hasta que todos los elegidos sean efectivamente llamados. Tenga en cuenta: (1.) Los pecadores están espiritualmente muertos, desprovistos de vida espiritual, sentido, fuerza y ​​movimiento, muertos para Dios, miserables, pero ni sensibles a su miseria ni capaces de ayudarse a sí mismos a salir de ella. (2.) La conversión de un alma a Dios es su resurrección de la muerte a la vida; luego comienza a vivir cuando comienza a vivir para Dios, a respirar tras Él y a avanzar hacia Él. (3.) Es por la voz del Hijo de Dios que las almas son elevadas a la vida espiritual; es obra de su poder, y ese poder es transmitido y comunicado por su palabra: Los muertos oirán, se les hará oír, comprender, recibir y creer la voz del Hijo de Dios, para oírla como su voz; entonces el Espíritu con él da vida; de lo contrario, la letra mata. (4.) Debemos escuchar la voz de Cristo para que podamos vivir de acuerdo con ella.

Los que oyen y atienden a lo que oyen, vivirán. Oye y tu alma vivirá, Isaías 55:3. En segundo lugar, una resurrección aún por venir; de esto se habla, Juan 5:28, Juan 5:29, introducido con: "No os maravilléis de esto que he dicho de la primera resurrección, no lo rechacéis como increíble y absurdo, porque al final de los tiempos todos veréis una prueba más sensible y sorprendente del poder y autoridad del Hijo del hombre". Así como su propia resurrección estaba reservada para ser la prueba final y concluyente de su comisión personal, así la resurrección de todos los hombres está reservada para ser una prueba similar de su comisión para ser ejecutada por su espíritu. Ahora observa aquí,
un. Cuando será esta resurrección: La hora viene; está fijado en una hora, por lo que es muy puntual esta gran cita. La sentencia no se aplaza sine die - hasta algún momento aún no fijado; no, él ha señalado un día. Se acerca la hora. (a.) Aún no ha llegado, no es la hora mencionada en Juan 5:25, la que viene, y ahora es. Se equivocaron peligrosamente los que dijeron que la resurrección ya había pasado, Ti 2:18, pero, (b.) Ciertamente vendrá, está llegando, cada día más cerca que otros; está en la puerta. No sabemos a qué distancia está; pero sabemos que está infaliblemente diseñado e inalterablemente determinado. b. Quién resucitará: Todos los que están en los sepulcros, todos los que han muerto desde el principio de los tiempos y todos los que morirán hasta el fin de los tiempos. Se dijo (Daniel 12:2): Muchos se levantarán; Cristo aquí nos dice que esos muchos serán todos; todos deben comparecer ante el Juez, y por tanto todos deben ser resucitados; cada persona y el conjunto de cada persona; cada alma volverá a su cuerpo, y cada hueso a su hueso. La tumba es la prisión de los cadáveres, donde son detenidos; su horno, donde se consumen (Job 24:19); sin embargo, en perspectiva de su resurrección, podemos llamarlo su cama, donde duermen para ser despertados nuevamente; su tesoro, donde se guardan para ser utilizados nuevamente. Incluso aquellos que no son sepultados se levantarán; pero, debido a que la mayoría son puestos en los sepulcros, Cristo usa esta expresión, todos los que están en los sepulcros. Los judíos usaban la palabra sheol para la tumba, que significa el estado de los muertos; todos los que están en ese estado oirán. do. Cómo serán resucitados.

Aquí se nos dicen dos cosas: - (a.) El efecto de esta resurrección: oirán su voz; es decir, les hará oírla, como a Lázaro se le hizo oír aquella palabra: Salid; un poder divino acompañará la voz, para darles vida y permitirles obedecerla. Cuando Cristo resucitó, no se escuchó ninguna voz, ni se pronunció una palabra, porque resucitó por su propio poder; pero en la resurrección de los hijos de los hombres encontramos que se habla de tres voces, 1 Tom 4:16. El Señor descenderá con voz de mando, con voz de rey, con voz de arcángel; ya sea el mismo Cristo, el príncipe de los ángeles, o el comandante en jefe, bajo su mando, de las huestes celestiales; y con la trompeta de Dios: la trompeta del soldado que da la alarma de la guerra, la trompeta del juez que publica la citación al tribunal. (b.) El efecto de ello: Saldrán de sus tumbas, como prisioneros de su prisión; se levantarán del polvo y se sacudirán de él; ver Isaías 52:1, Isaías 52:2, Isaías 52:11. Pero esto no es todo; comparecerán ante el tribunal de Cristo, se presentarán como aquellos que van a ser juzgados, se presentarán ante el tribunal, públicamente para recibir su condena. d. A qué serán elevados; a diferente estado de felicidad o miseria, según su diferente carácter; a un estado de retribución, según lo que hicieron en el estado de prueba. (a.) Los que han hecho el bien saldrán a la resurrección de vida; vivirán de nuevo, para vivir para siempre. Tenga en cuenta, [a.] Cualquiera que sea el nombre con el que se llame a los hombres, o cualquier profesión plausible que hagan, en el gran día les irá bien sólo a aquellos que hayan hecho el bien, hayan hecho lo que agrada a Dios y es provechoso para los demás. [b.] La resurrección de la carne será resurrección de vida para todos aquellos, y sólo para aquellos, que han sido sinceros y constantes en hacer el bien. No sólo serán absueltos públicamente, como decimos que un criminal perdonado tiene su vida, sino que serán admitidos en la presencia de Dios, y eso es vida, es mejor que la vida; serán atendidos con comodidades en perfección. Vivir es ser feliz, y superarán el miedo a la muerte; así es realmente la vida en la que la mortalidad es absorbida para siempre. (b.) Los que han hecho mal, para resurrección de condenación; vivirán de nuevo y morirán para siempre.

Los fariseos pensaban que la resurrección pertenecía sólo a los justos, pero aquí Cristo rectifica ese error. Tenga en cuenta, [a.] Los malhechores, sea lo que fuere lo que pretendan, serán tratados en el día del juicio como hombres malvados. [b.] La resurrección será para los malhechores, que mediante el arrepentimiento no deshicieron lo que habían hecho mal, una resurrección de condenación. Saldrán para ser condenados públicamente de rebelión contra Dios y condenados públicamente al castigo eterno; ser sentenciado a ello, y enviado inmediatamente a él sin indulto. Así será la resurrección. (2.) Observe lo que se dice aquí sobre la autoridad del Mediador para ejecutar juicio, Juan 5:22-24, Juan 5:27. Así como tiene un poder todopoderoso, también tiene una jurisdicción soberana; ¿Y quién tan apto para presidir los grandes asuntos de la otra vida como él que es Padre y fuente de vida? Aquí está,
[1.] La comisión o delegación de Cristo al cargo de juez, de la que se habla dos veces aquí (Juan 5:22): ha confiado todo juicio al Hijo; y otra vez (Juan 5:27): le ha dado autoridad. Primero, el Padre a nadie juzga; no es que el Padre haya renunciado al gobierno, sino que se complace en gobernar por Jesucristo; de modo que el hombre no esté bajo el terror de tratar con Dios inmediatamente, sino que tenga el consuelo de acceder a él a través de un Mediador. Habiéndonos creado, puede hacer con nosotros lo que quiera, como el alfarero con el barro; sin embargo, él no se aprovecha de esto, sino que nos atrae con cuerdas de hombre. 2. Él no determina nuestra condición eterna por el pacto de inocencia, ni aprovecha la ventaja que tiene contra nosotros por la violación de ese pacto. Una vez que el Mediador se ha comprometido a lograr una satisfacción vicaria, se le remite el asunto y Dios está dispuesto a celebrar un nuevo tratado; no bajo la ley del Creador, sino la gracia del Redentor. En segundo lugar, ha confiado todo el juicio al Hijo, lo ha constituido Señor de todo (Hch 10,36; Rom 14,9), como José en Egipto, Gn 41,40. Esto fue profetizado, Salmo 72:1; Isaías 11:3, Isaías 11:4; Jeremías 23:5; Miqueas 5:1-4; Salmo 67:4; Sal 96:13; Sal 98:9. Todo juicio está encomendado a nuestro Señor Jesús; porque 1. A él se le ha confiado la administración del reino providencial, es cabeza sobre todas las cosas (Efesios 1:11), cabeza de todo hombre, 1 Col 11:3. Todas las cosas consisten en él, Col 1:17. 2. Tiene poder para dictar leyes inmediatamente para obligar a la conciencia.

Os digo que es ahora la forma en que corren las estatuas del reino de los cielos. Sea promulgado por el Señor Jesús y por su autoridad. Todos los actos ahora vigentes son tocados con su cetro. 3. Está autorizado para nombrar y fijar los términos del nuevo pacto, y redactar los artículos de paz entre Dios y los hombres; es Dios en Cristo quien reconcilia al mundo, y a él le ha dado poder para conferir la vida eterna. El libro de la vida es el libro del Cordero; por su premio debemos permanecer firmes o caer. 4. Tiene el encargo de continuar y completar la guerra contra los poderes de las tinieblas; para echar fuera y dictar sentencia contra el príncipe de este mundo, Juan 12:31. Tiene el encargo no sólo de juzgar, sino también de hacer la guerra, Apocalipsis 19:11. Todos los que quieran luchar por Dios contra Satanás deben alistarse bajo su bandera. 5. Se constituye administrador único del juicio del gran día. Los antiguos generalmente entendían estas palabras de ese acto culminante de su poder judicial. El juicio final y universal está encomendado al Hijo del hombre; el tribunal es suyo, es el tribunal de Cristo; suyo es el séquito, sus ángeles poderosos; probará las causas y dictará sentencia. Hechos 17:31. En tercer lugar, también le ha dado autoridad para ejecutar juicio, Juan 5:27. Observe, 1. Cuál es la autoridad que tiene nuestro Redentor: una autoridad para ejecutar juicio; no sólo tiene poder legislativo y judicial, sino también poder ejecutivo. La frase aquí se usa particularmente para el juicio de condenación, Jde 1:15. poiēsai krisin - para ejecutar juicio sobre todos; lo mismo con su venganza, 2 Tom 1:8. La ruina de los pecadores impenitentes viene de la mano de Cristo; el que ejecuta juicio sobre ellos es el mismo que les habría producido la salvación, lo que hace que la sentencia sea intachable; y no hay remedio contra la sentencia del Redentor; la salvación misma no puede salvar a aquellos a quienes el Salvador condena, lo que hace que la ruina sea irremediable. 2. De dónde tiene esa autoridad: el Padre se la dio. La autoridad de Cristo como Mediador se delega y se deriva; actúa como Vicerregente del Padre, como el Ungido del Señor, el Cristo del Señor.

Ahora bien, todo esto redunda mucho en honor de Cristo, eximiéndolo de la culpa de blasfemia, haciéndose igual a Dios; y para gran consuelo de todos los creyentes, quienes con la mayor seguridad pueden arriesgar todo en tales manos. [2.] Aquí están las razones (razones de estado) por las cuales se le dio esta comisión. Tiene todo el juicio confiado a él por dos razones: - 
Primero, porque es el Hijo del hombre; que denota estas tres cosas: - 1. Su humillación y graciosa condescendencia. El hombre es un gusano, el hijo del hombre un gusano; sin embargo, esta fue la naturaleza, este el carácter que asumió el Redentor, en cumplimiento de los consejos de amor; a esta baja condición se rebajó y se sometió a todas las mortificaciones que la acompañaban, porque era la voluntad de su Padre; Por tanto, en recompensa de esta maravillosa obediencia, Dios lo dignificó así. Debido a que condescendió a ser Hijo del hombre, su Padre lo hizo Señor de todos, Filipenses 2:8, Filipenses 2:9. 2. Su afinidad y alianza con nosotros. El Padre le ha encomendado el gobierno de los hijos de los hombres, porque, siendo Hijo del hombre, es de la misma naturaleza que aquellos sobre quienes está bajo su autoridad, y por lo tanto es más intachable y más aceptable como Juez. Su gobernador procederá de en medio de ellos, Jeremias 30:21. De esto esa ley era típica; A uno de tus hermanos pondrás rey sobre ti, Deuteronomio 17:15. 3. Ser el Mesías prometido. En esa famosa visión de su reino y gloria, Dan 7:13, Dan 7:14, se le llama Hijo del hombre; y Salmo 8:4-6. Tú has hecho que el Hijo del Hombre tenga señorío sobre las obras de tus manos. Él es el Mesías y, por tanto, está investido de todo este poder. Los judíos solían llamar a Cristo el Hijo de David; pero Cristo generalmente se llamaba a sí mismo Hijo del hombre, que era el título más humilde, y lo presenta como príncipe y Salvador, no sólo para la nación judía, sino para toda la raza humana. En segundo lugar, que todos los hombres honren al Hijo, Juan 5:23. Aquí se habla de honrar a Jesucristo como el gran diseño de Dios (el Hijo tenía la intención de glorificar al Padre, y por lo tanto el Padre tenía la intención de glorificar al Hijo, Juan 12:32); y como gran deber del hombre, en cumplimiento de ese designio. Si Dios quiere que el Hijo sea honrado, es deber de todos aquellos a quienes se le da a conocer honrarlo. Observe aquí, 1.

El respeto que se debe rendir a nuestro Señor Jesús: debemos honrar al Hijo, debemos considerarlo como alguien que debe ser honrado, tanto por sus excelencias y perfecciones trascendentes en sí mismo como por las relaciones que mantiene con nosotros, y debemos estudiar para honrarlo en consecuencia; debe confesar que él es Señor y adorarlo; debemos honrar al que por nosotros fue deshonrado. 2. El grado de la misma: así como honran al Padre. Esto supone que es nuestro deber honrar al Padre; porque la religión revelada se funda en la religión natural y nos dirige a honrar al Hijo, a honrarlo con honor divino; debemos honrar al Redentor con el mismo honor con el que honramos al Creador. Estaba tan lejos de ser una blasfemia que él se hiciera igual a Dios que es el mayor daño que puede ser para nosotros hacerle lo contrario. Las verdades y leyes de la religión cristiana, en la medida en que son reveladas, son tan sagradas y honorables como las de la religión natural, y deben ser igualmente estimadas; porque tenemos las mismas obligaciones para con Cristo, el Autor de nuestro ser; y tener una dependencia tan necesaria de la gracia del Redentor como de la providencia del Creador, que es base suficiente para esta ley: honrar al Hijo como honramos al Padre. Para hacer cumplir esta ley, se añade: El que no honra al Hijo, no honra al Padre que lo envió. Algunos pretenden reverenciar al Creador y hablan con honor de él, mientras que se burlan del Redentor y hablan de él con desprecio; pero que sepan que los honores e intereses del Padre y del Hijo están tan inseparablemente retorcidos y entrelazados que el Padre nunca se considera honrado por nadie que deshonre al Hijo. Nota: (1.) Las indignidades cometidas contra el Señor Jesús se reflejan en Dios mismo, y así serán interpretadas y contabilizadas en el tribunal del cielo. Habiendo el Hijo abrazado el honor del Padre hasta el punto de tomar para sí los reproches que se le hacen (Romanos 15:3), el Padre no menos abraza el honor del Hijo, y se considera herido a través de él. (2.) La razón de esto es que el Hijo es enviado y comisionado por el Padre; es el Padre quien lo ha enviado. Las afrentas a un embajador son justamente resentidas por el príncipe que lo envía. Y por esta regla los que verdaderamente honran al Hijo honran también al Padre; ver Filipenses 2:11.

[3.] Aquí está la regla por la cual el Hijo ejecuta esta comisión, por lo que esas palabras parecen entrar (Juan 5:24): El que oye y cree, tiene vida eterna. Aquí tenemos la sustancia de todo el evangelio; el prefacio exige atención a algo muy importante y asentimiento a algo muy cierto: "De cierto, de cierto os digo, yo, a quien oísteis que se encomienda todo juicio, yo, en cuyos labios hay una sentencia divina; quitad de mí el carácter y la carta del cristiano".
Primero, el carácter del cristiano: el que oye mi palabra y cree en el que me envió. Ser cristiano en verdad es: 1. Escuchar la palabra de Cristo. No basta con escucharlo, sino que debemos prestar atención a él, como eruditos siguiendo las instrucciones de sus maestros; y atenderlo, como sirvientes a las órdenes de sus amos; debemos oírlo y obedecerlo, debemos acatar el evangelio de Cristo como regla fija de nuestra fe y práctica. 2. Creer en el que lo envió; porque el diseño de Cristo es llevarnos a Dios; y, así como él es el primer original de toda gracia, también es el último objeto de toda fe. Cristo es nuestro camino; Dios es nuestro descanso. Debemos creer en Dios que envió a Jesucristo y se recomendó a nuestra fe y amor, manifestando su gloria en el rostro de Jesucristo (Co 2 4:6), como su Padre y nuestro Padre. En segundo lugar, la Carta de un cristiano, en la que todos los que son cristianos están interesados. Vea lo que obtenemos de Cristo. 1. Carta de perdón: no vendrá a condenación. La gracia del evangelio es una liberación total de la maldición de la ley. Un creyente no sólo no estará bajo condenación eterna, sino que no vendrá a condenación ahora, no correrá el peligro de ello (Romanos 8:1), no será juzgado, ni siquiera será procesado. 2. Una carta de privilegios: Pasa de la muerte a la vida, es investido de una felicidad presente en la vida espiritual y tiene derecho a una felicidad futura en la vida eterna. El tenor del primer pacto fue: Haz esto y vive; el hombre que las hace vivirá en ellas. Ahora bien, esto prueba que Cristo es igual al Padre en que tiene poder para proponer a los oyentes de su palabra el mismo beneficio que había sido propuesto a los guardianes de la antigua ley, es decir, la vida: Oír y vivir, creer y vivir, es a lo que podemos aventurar nuestras almas, cuando estamos incapacitados para hacer y vivir; ver Juan 17:2.

[4.] Aquí está la justicia de sus procedimientos de conformidad con esta comisión, Juan 5:30. Dado que todo el juicio se le ha confiado, no podemos dejar de preguntarnos cómo lo gestiona. Y aquí él responde: Mi juicio es justo. Todo Cristo

b17.en:
In these verses our Lord Jesus proves and confirms the commission he had produced, and makes it out that he was sent of God to be the Messiah.
I. He sets aside his own testimony of himself (Joh 5:31): "If I bear witness of myself, though it is infallibly true (Joh 8:14), yet, according to the common rule of judgment among men, you will not admit it as legal proof, nor allow it to be given in evidence." Now, 1. This reflects reproach upon the sons of men, and their veracity and integrity. Surely we may say deliberately, what David said in haste, All men are liars, else it would never have been such a received maxim that a man's testimony of himself is suspicious, and not to be relied on; it is a sign that self-love is stronger than the love of truth. And yet, 2. It reflects honour on the Son of God, and bespeaks his wonderful condescension, that, though he is the faithful witness, the truth itself, who may challenge to be credited upon his honour, and his own single testimony, yet he is pleased to waive his privilege, and, for the confirmation of our faith, refers himself to his vouchers, that we may have full satisfaction.
II. He produces other witnesses that bear testimony to him that he was sent of God.
1. The Father himself bore testimony to him (Joh 5:32): There is another that beareth witness. I take this to be meant of God the Father, for Christ mentions his testimony with his own (Joh 8:18): I bear witness of myself, and the Father beareth witness of me. Observe,
(1.) The seal which the Father put to his commission: He beareth witness of me, not only has done so by a voice from heaven, but still does so by the tokens of his presence with me. See who they are to whom God will bear witness. [1.] Those whom he sends and employs; where he gives commissions he give credentials. [2.] Those who bear witness to him; so Christ did. God will own and honour those that own and honour him. [3.] Those who decline bearing witness of themselves; so Christ did. God will take care that those who humble and abase themselves, and seek not their own glory, shall not lose by it.
(2.) The satisfaction Christ had in this testimony: "I know that the witness which he witnesseth of me is true. I am very well assured that I have a divine mission, and do not in the least hesitate concerning it; thus he had the witness in himself." The devil tempted him to question his being the Son of God, but he never yielded.
2. John Baptist witnessed to Christ, Joh 5:33, etc. John came to bear witness of the light (Joh 1:7); his business was to prepare his way, and direct people to him: Behold the Lamb of God.
(1.) Now the testimony of John was, [1.] A solemn and public testimony: "You sent an embassy of priests and Levites to John, which gave him an opportunity of publishing what he had to say; it was not a popular, but a judicial testimony." [2.] It was a true testimony: He bore witness to the truth, as a witness ought to do, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Christ does not say, He bore witness to me (though every one knew he did), but, like an honest man, He bore witness to the truth. Now John was confessedly such a holy, good man, so mortified to the world, and so conversant with divine things, that it could not be imagined he should be guilty of such a forgery and imposture as to say what he did concerning Christ if it had not been so, and if he had not been sure of it.
(2.) Two things are added concerning John's testimony: - 
[1.] That it was a testimony ex abundanti - more than he needed to vouch (Joh 5:34): I receive not testimony from man. Though Christ saw fit to quote John's testimony, it was with a protestation that it shall not be deemed or construed so as to prejudice the prerogative of his self-sufficiency. Christ needs no letters or commendation, no testimonials or certificates, but what his own worth and excellency bring with him; why then did Christ here urge the testimony of John? Why, these things I say, that you may be saved. This he aimed at in all this discourse, to save not his own life, but the souls of others; he produced John's testimony because, being one of themselves, it was to be hoped that they would hearken to it. Note, First, Christ desires and designs the salvation even of his enemies and persecutors. Secondly, The word of Christ is the ordinary means of salvation. Thirdly, Christ in his word considers our infirmities and condescends to our capacities, consulting not so much what it befits so great a prince to say as what we can bear, and what will be most likely to do us good.
[2.] That it was a testimony ad hominem - to the man, because John Baptist was one whom they had a respect for (Joh 5:35): He was a light among you.
First, The character of John Baptist: He was a burning and a shining light. Christ often spoke honourably of John; he was now in prison under a cloud, yet Christ gives him his due praise, which we must be ready to do to all that faithfully serve God. 1. He was a light, not phōs - lux, light (so Christ was the light), but luknos - lucerna, a luminary, a derived subordinate light. His office was to enlighten a dark world with notices of the Messiah's approach, to whom he was as the morning star. 2. He was a burning light, which denotes sincerity; painted fire may be made to shine, but that which burns is true fire. It denotes also his activity, zeal, and fervency, burning in love to God and the souls of men; fire is always working on itself or something else, so is a good minister. 3. He was a shining light, which denotes either his exemplary conversation, in which our light should shine (Mat 5:16), or an eminent diffusive influence. He was illustrious in the sight of others; though he affected obscurity and retirement, and was in the deserts, yet such were his doctrine, his baptism, his life, that he became very remarkable, and attracted the eyes of the nation.
Secondly, The affections of the people to him: you were willing for a season to rejoice in his light. 1. It was a transport that they were in, upon the appearing of John: "You were willing - ēthelēsate, you delighted to rejoice in his light; you were very proud that you had such a man among you, who was the honour of your country; you were willing agalliasthēnai - willing to dance, and make a noise about this light, as boys about a bonfire." 2. It was but transient, and soon over: "You were fond of him, pros hōran - for an hour, for a season, as little children are fond of a new thing, you were pleased with John awhile, but soon grew weary of him and his ministry, and said that he had a devil, and now you have him in prison." Note, Many, that seem to be affected and pleased with the gospel at first, afterwards despise and reject it; it is common for forward and noisy professors to cool and fall off. These here rejoiced in John's light, but never walked in it, and therefore did not keep to it; they were like the stony ground. While Herod was a friend to John Baptist, the people caressed him; but when he fell under Herod's frowns he lost their favours: "You were willing to countenance John, pros hōran that is, for temporal ends" (so some take it); "you were glad of him, in hopes to make a tool of him, by his interest and under the shelter of his name to have shaken off the Roman yoke, and recovered the civil liberty and honour of your country." Now, (1.) Christ mentions their respect to John, to condemn them for their present opposition to himself, to whom John bore witness. If they had continued their veneration for John, as they ought to have done, they would have embraced Christ. (2.) He mentions the passing away of their respect, to justify God in depriving them, as he had now done, of John's ministry, and putting that light under a bushel.
3. Christ's own works witnessed to him (Joh 5:36): I have a testimony greater than that of John; for if we believe the witness of men sent of God, as John was, the witness of God immediately, and not by the ministry of men, is greater, Jo1 5:9. Observe, Though the witness of John was a less cogent and less considerable witness, yet our Lord was pleased to make use of it. We must be glad of all the supports that offer themselves for the confirmation of our faith, though they may not amount to a demonstration, and we must not invalidate any, under pretence that there are others more conclusive; we have occasion for them all. Now this greater testimony was that of the works which his Father had given him to finish. That is, (1.) In general the whole course of his life and ministry - his revealing God and his will to us, setting up his kingdom among men, reforming the world, destroying Satan's kingdom, restoring fallen man to his primitive purity and felicity, and shedding abroad in men's hearts the love of God and of one another - all that work of which he said when he died, It is finished, it was all, from first to last, opus Deo dignum - a work worthy of God; all he said and did was holy and heavenly, and a divine purity, power, and grace shone in it, proving abundantly that he was sent of God. (2.) In particular. The miracles he wrought for the proof of his divine mission witnessed of him. Now it is here said, [1.] That these works were given him by the Father, that is, he was both appointed and empowered to work them; for, as Mediator, he derived both commission and strength from his Father. [2.] They were given to him to finish; he must do all those works of wonder which the counsel and foreknowledge of God had before determined to be done; and his finishing them proves a divine power; for as for God his work is perfect. [3.] These works did bear witness of him, did prove that he was sent of God, and that what he said concerning himself was true; see Heb 2:4; Act 2:22. That the Father had sent him as a Father, not as a master sends his servant on an errand, but as a father sends his son to take possession for himself; if God had not sent him, he would not have seconded him, would not have sealed him, as he did by the works he gave him to do; for the world's Creator will never be its deceiver.
4. He produces, more fully than before, his Father's testimony concerning him (Joh 5:37): The Father that sent me hath borne witness of me. The prince is not accustomed to follow his ambassador himself, to confirm his commission viva voce - by speaking; but God was pleased to bear witness of his Son himself by a voice from heaven at his baptism (Mat 3:17): This is my ambassador, This is my beloved Son. The Jews reckoned Batḣkol; - the daughter of a voice, a voice from heaven, one of the ways by which God made known his mind; and in that way he had owned Christ publicly and solemnly, and repeated it, Mat 17:5. Note, (1.) Those whom God sends he will bear witness of; where he gives a commission, he will not fail to seal it; he that never left himself without witness (Act 14:17) will never leave any of his servants so, who go upon his errand. (2.) Where God demands belief, he will not fail to give sufficient evidence, as he has done concerning Christ. That which was to be witnessed concerning Christ was chiefly this, that the God we had offended was willing to accept of him as a Mediator. Now concerning this he has himself given us full satisfaction (and he was fittest to do it), declaring himself well-pleased in him; if we be so, the work is done. Now, it might be suggested, if God himself thus bore witness of Christ, how came it to pass that he was not universally received by the Jewish nation and their rulers? To this Christ here answers that it was not to be thought strange, nor could their infidelity weaken his credibility, for two reasons: - [1.] Because they were not acquainted with such extraordinary revelations of God and his will: You have neither heard his voice at any time, nor seen his shape, or appearance. They showed themselves to be as ignorant of God, though they professed relation to him, as we are of a man we never either saw or heard. "But why do I talk to you of God's bearing witness of me? He is one you know nothing of, nor have any acquaintance or communion with." Note, Ignorance of God is the true reason of men's rejecting the record he has given concerning his Son. A right understanding of natural religion would discover to us such admirable congruities in the Christian religion as would greatly dispose our minds to the entertainment of it. Some give this sense of it: "The Father bore witness of me by a voice, and the descent of a dove, which is such an extraordinary thing that you never saw or heard the like; and yet for my sake there was such a voice and appearance; yea, and you might have heard that voice, you might have seen that appearance, as others did, if you had closely attended the ministry of John, but by slighting it you missed of that testimony." [2.] Because they were not affected, no, not with the ordinary ways by which God had revealed himself to them: You have not his word abiding in you, Joh 5:38. They had the scriptures of the Old Testament; might they not by them be disposed to receive Christ? Yes, if they had had their due influence upon them. But, First, The word of God was not in them; it was among them, in their country, in their hands, but not in them, in their hearts; not ruling in their souls, but only shining in their eyes and sounding in their ears. What did it avail them that they had the oracles of God committed to them (Rom 3:2), when they had not these oracles commanding in them? If they had, they would readily have embraced Christ. Secondly, It did not abide. Many have the word of God coming into them, and making some impressions for awhile, but it does not abide with them; it is not constantly in them, as a man at home, but only now and then, as a wayfaring man. If the word abide in us, if we converse with it by frequent meditation, consult with it upon every occasion, and conform to it in our conversation, we shall then readily receive the witness of the Father concerning Christ; see Joh 7:17. But how did it appear that they had not the word of God abiding in them? It appeared by this, Whom he hath sent, him ye believe not. There was so much said in the Old Testament concerning Christ, to direct people when and where to look for him, and so to facilitate the discovery of him, that, if they had duly considered these things, they could not have avoided the conviction of Christ's being sent of God; so that their not believing in Christ was a certain sign that the word of God did not abide in them. Note, The in-dwelling of the word, and Spirit, and grace of God in us, is best tried by its effects, particularly by our receiving what he sends, the commands, the messengers, the providences he sends, especially Christ whom he hath sent.
5. The last witness he calls is the Old Testament, which witnessed of him, and to it he appeals (Joh 5:39, etc.): Search the scriptures, ereunate.
(1.) This may be read, either, [1.] "You search the scriptures, and you do well to do so; you read them daily in your synagogues, you have rabbies, and doctors, and scribes, that make it their business to study them, and criticize upon them." The Jews boasted of the flourishing of scripture-learning in the days of Hillel, who died about twelve years after Christ's birth, and reckoned some of those who were then members of the sanhedrim the beauties of their wisdom and the glories of their law; and Christ owns that they did indeed search the scriptures, but it was in search of their own glory: "You search the scriptures, and therefore, if you were not wilfully blind, you would believe in me." Note, It is possible for men to be very studious in the letter of the scripture, and yet to be strangers to the power and influence of it. Or, [2.] As we read it: Search the scriptures; and so, First, It was spoken to them in the nature of an appeal: "You profess to receive and believe the scripture; here I will join issue with you, let this be the judge, provided you will not rest in the letter" (haerere in cortice), "but will search into it." Note, when appeals are made to the scriptures, they must be searched. Search the whole book of scripture throughout, compare one passage with another, and explain one by another. We must likewise search particular passages to the bottom, and see not what they seem to say prima facie - at the first appearance, but what they say indeed. Secondly, It is spoken to us in the nature of an advice, or a command to all Christians to search the scriptures. Note, All those who would find Christ must search the scriptures; not only read them, and hear them, but search them, which denotes, 1. Diligence in seeking, labour, and study, and close application of mind. 2. Desire and design of finding. We must aim at some spiritual benefit and advantage in reading and studying the scripture, and often ask, "What am I now searching for?" We must search as for hidden treasures (Pro 2:4), as those that sink for gold or silver, or that dive for pearl, Job 28:1-11. This ennobled the Bereans, Act 17:11.
(2.) Now there are two things which we are here directed to have in our eye, in our searching the scripture: heaven our end, and Christ our way. [1.] We must search the scriptures for heaven as our great end: For in them you think you have eternal life. The scripture assures us of an eternal state set before us, and offers to us an eternal life in that state: it contains the chart that describes it, the charter that conveys it, the direction in the way that leads to it, and the foundation upon which the hope of it is built; and this is worth searching for where we are sure to find it. But to the Jews Christ saith only, You think you have eternal life in the scriptures, because, though they did retain the belief and hope of eternal life, and grounded their expectations of it upon the scriptures, yet herein they missed it, that they looked for it by the bare reading and studying of the scripture. It was a common but corrupt saying among them, He that has the words of the law has eternal life; they thought they were sure of heaven if they could say by heart, or rather by rote, such and such passages of scripture as they were directed to by the tradition of the elders; as they thought all the vulgar cursed because they did not thus know the law (Joh 7:49), so they concluded all the learned undoubtedly blessed. [2.] We must search the scriptures for Christ, as the new and living way that leads to this end. These are they, the great and principal witnesses, that testify of me. Note, First, The scriptures, even those of the Old Testament, testify of Christ, and by them God bears witness to him. The Spirit of Christ in the prophets testified beforehand of him (Pe1 1:11), the purposes and promises of God concerning him, and the previous notices of him. The Jews knew very well that the Old Testament testified of the Messiah, and were critical in their remarks upon the passages that looked that way; and yet were careless, and wretchedly overseen, in the application of them. Secondly, Therefore we must search the scriptures, and may hope to find eternal life in that search, because they testify of Christ; for this is life eternal, to know him; see Jo1 5:11. Christ is the treasure hid in the field of the scriptures, the water in those wells, the milk in those breasts.
(3.) To this testimony he annexes a reproof of their infidelity and wickedness in four instances; particularly,
[1.] Their neglect of him and his doctrine: "You will not come tome, that you might have life, Joh 5:40. You search the scriptures, you believe the prophets, who you cannot but see testify of me; and yet you will not come to me, to whom they direct you." Their estrangement from Christ was the fault not so much of their understandings as of their wills. This is expressed as a complaint; Christ offered life, and it was not accepted. Note, First, There is life to be had with Jesus Christ for poor souls; we may have life, the life of pardon and grace, and comfort and glory: life is the perfection of our being, and inclusive of all happiness; and Christ is our life. Secondly, Those that would have this life must come to Jesus Christ for it; we may have it for the coming for. It supposes an assent of the understanding to the doctrine of Christ and the record given concerning him; it lies in the consent of the will to his government and grace, and it produces an answerable compliance in the affections and actions. Thirdly, The only reason why sinners die is because they will not come to Christ for life and happiness; it is not because they cannot, but because they will not. They will neither accept the life offered, because spiritual and divine, nor will they agree to the terms on which it is offered, nor apply themselves to the use of the appointed means: they will not be cured, for they will not observe the methods of cure. Fourthly, The wilfulness and obstinacy of sinners in rejecting the tenders of grace are a great grief to the Lord Jesus, and what he complains of. Those words (Joh 5:41), I receive not honour from men, come in a parenthesis, to obviate an objection against him, as if he sought his own glory, and made himself the head of a party, in obliging all to come to him, and applaud him. Note, 1. He did not covet nor court the applause of men, did not in the least affect that worldly pomp and splendour in which the carnal Jews expected their Messiah to appear. He charged those whom he cured not to make him known, and withdrew from those that would have made him king. 2. He had not the applause of men. Instead of receiving honour from men, he received a great deal of dishonour and disgrace from men, for he made himself of no reputation. 3. He needed not the applause of men; it was no addition to his glory whom all the angels of God worship, nor was he any otherwise pleased with it than as it was according to his Father's will, and for the happiness of those who, in giving honour to him, received much greater honour from him.
[2.] Their want of the love of God (Joh 5:42): "I know you very well, that you have not the love of God in you. Why should I wonder that you do not come to me, when you want even the first principle of natural religion, which is the love of God?" Note, The reason why people slight Christ is because they do not love God; for, if we did indeed love God, we should love him who is his express image, and hasten to him by whom only we may be restored to the favour of God. He charged them (Joh 5:37) with ignorance of God, and here with want of love to him; therefore men have not the love of God because they desire not the knowledge of him. Observe, First, The crime charged upon them: You have not the love of God in you. They pretended a great love to God, and thought they proved it by their zeal for the law, the temple, and the sabbath; and yet they were really without the love of God. Note, There are many who make a great profession of religion who yet show they want the love of God by their neglect of Christ and their contempt of his commandments; they hate his holiness and undervalue his goodness. Observe, It is the love of God in us, that love seated in the heart, a living active principle there, that God will accept; the love shed abroad there, Rom 5:5. Secondly, The proof of this charge, by the personal knowledge of Christ, who searches the heart (Rev 2:23) and knows what is in man: I know you. Christ sees through all our disguises, and can say to each of us, I know thee. 1. Christ knows men better than their neighbours know them. The people thought that the scribes and Pharisees were very devout and good men, but Christ knew that they had not the love of God in them. 2. Christ knows men better than they know themselves. These Jews had a very good opinion of themselves, but Christ knew how corrupt their inside was, notwithstanding the speciousness of their outside; we may deceive ourselves, but we cannot deceive him. 3. Christ knows men who do not, and will not, know him; he looks on those who industriously look off from him, and calls by their own name, their true name, those who have not known him.
[3.] Another crime charged upon them is their readiness to entertain false Christs and false prophets, while they obstinately opposed him who was the true Messias (Joh 5:43): I am come in my Father's name, and you receive me not. If another shall come in his own name, him you will receive. Be astonished, O heavens, at this (Jer 2:12, Jer 2:13); for my people have committed two evils, great evils indeed. First, They have forsaken the fountain of living waters, for they would not receive Christ, who came in his Father's name, had his commission from his Father, and did all for his glory. Secondly, They have hewn out broken cisterns, they hearken to every one that will set up in his own name. They forsake their own mercies, which is bad enough; and it is for lying vanities, which is worse. observe here, 1. Those are false prophets who come in their own name, who run without being sent, and set up for themselves only. 2. It is just with God to suffer those to be deceived with false prophets who receive not the truth in the love of it. Th2 2:10, Th2 2:11. The errors of antichrist are the just punishment of those who obey not the doctrine of Christ. They that shut their eyes against the true light are by the judgment of God given up to wander endlessly after false lights, and to be led aside after every ignis fatuus. 3. It is the gross folly of many that, while they nauseate ancient truths, they are fond of upstart errors; they loathe manna, and at the same time feed upon ashes. After the Jews had rejected Christ and his gospel, they were continually haunted with spectres, with false Christs and false prophets (Mat 24:24), and their proneness to follow such occasioned those distractions and seditions that hastened their ruin.
[4.] They are here charged with pride and vain-glory, and unbelief, the effect of them, Joh 5:44. Having sharply reproved their unbelief, like a wise physician, he here searches into the cause, lays the axe to the root. They therefore slighted and undervalued Christ because they admired and overvalued themselves. Here is,
First, Their ambition of worldly honour. Christ despised it, Joh 5:41. They set their hearts upon it: You receive honour one of another; that is, "You look for a Messiah in outward pomp, and promise yourselves worldly honour by him." You receive honour: - 1. "You desire to receive it, and aim at this in all you do." 2. "You give honour to others, and applaud them, only that they may return it, and may applaud you." Petimus dabimusque vicissim - We ask and we bestow. It is the proud man's art to throw honour upon others only that it may rebound upon himself. 3. "You are very careful to keep all the honours to yourselves, and confine them to your own party, as if you had the monopoly of that which is honourable." 4. "What respect is shown to you you receive yourselves, and do not transmit to God, as Herod." Idolizing men and their sentiments, and affecting to be idolized by them and their applauses, are pieces of idolatry as directly contrary to Christianity as any other.
Secondly, Their neglect of spiritual honour, called here the honour that comes from God only; this they sought not, nor minded. Note, 1. True honour is that which comes from God only, that is real and lasting honour; those are honourable indeed whom he takes into covenant and communion with himself. 2. This honour have all the saints. All that believe in Christ, through him receive the honour that comes from God. He is not partial, but will give glory wherever he gives grace. 3. This honour that comes from God we must seek, must aim at it, and act for it, and take up with nothing short of it (Rom 2:29); we must account it our reward, as the Pharisees accounted the praise of men. 4.
